entries.author: ivy
entries.caption: The station with no clocks
entries.narration: At the last stop, the conductor gave me a paper ticket with a leaf pressed inside. The platform had no clocks. Every bench faced a little orchard. I sat there until a pear dropped into my coat pocket. That was my train home.
replies: thea
A pear instead of a departure bell. I hope that train takes the long way.
iris
Keeping the leaf ticket is my favorite part.

entries.author: june
entries.caption: Watching the streetlights melt into the rain. Which color do you notice first?
replies: ivy
The little gold one that disappears behind the next drop.

entries.author: bea
entries.caption: A shell with a front door
entries.narration: There was a blue door in the side of a seashell. Inside, someone had put a kettle on. We drank tea at a table small enough to fit between two waves. When I woke up, I could almost hear the cups settling back into their saucers.
replies: wren
Two cups on a tiny table. That detail stayed with me.
clea
I would love to know what kind of tea the sea makes.

entries.author: clea
entries.caption: Twelve seconds at the edge of the water. The foam draws a different little map each time.
replies: bea
That thin bright line just before the water retreats.
thea
I watched twice for the second wave.

entries.author: wren
entries.caption: The staircase played a tune
entries.narration: The stairs in my dream made a different note with every step. I tried to climb quietly, but the house hummed along anyway. Halfway up I sat down. A blackbird on the banister finished the tune for me.
replies: june
I can picture the bird waiting for its cue.

entries.author: nell
entries.caption: A cloud borrowed the moon for a moment. Watch the bright edge on the right.
replies: wren
The cloud looks like a curtain lifting.
iris
The little pause before the moon comes back is lovely.

entries.author: iris
entries.caption: Postcards in a paper boat
entries.narration: I folded an old street map into a boat and set it on a puddle. It came back carrying a postcard. On the front was my own window, lit from inside. On the back, in very small letters, someone had written, You can take the slow way.
replies: nell
I would pin that postcard over my desk.

entries.author: thea
entries.caption: The ferry that carried stars
entries.narration: The last ferry crossed a lake so still that the stars seemed to be floating on it. The deckhand scooped one up with a teacup. He set it on the railing, where it gave us just enough light to read our books all the way across.
replies: ivy
Just enough light for a book sounds perfect.
bea
I am still thinking about that teacup.

rooms.title: The Last Stop
rooms.topic: Night Journal · Leave a line about the quietest part of your day.
notes: Tonight’s prompt: what small sound tells you the day is over?
The click when the kitchen light goes out.
For me it is the ferry bell carrying over the water.

rooms.title: Low Tide Letters
rooms.topic: Night Journal · A place to trade little notes from the shore.
notes: If you could leave a note in a shell, what would it say?
The tide will bring you another clean page.
Mine would have a tiny map folded inside.

rooms.title: The Humming Window
rooms.topic: Night Journal · Share a tune, a rain sound or a bedtime ritual.
notes: One sound for a bedtime playlist: a spoon tapping the rim of a cup.
A window latch, followed by the first few drops of rain.
